findings.title: Connection dropdown reads group_id, which is not a field in 5 actions
findings.location: <each action> › V1 › inputjson › connection_id › optionsGenerator / source, and blocks.connection_id.dependsOn
findings.issue: The dropdown calls listFivetranConnections(context?.inputData?.group_id, ...) but these actions have no group_id field, so dependsOn lists a parent that never exists. The list is never filtered and, in the editor, the dropdown may wait for a parent value that cannot be set (not verified in the UI).

evidence.ref: Sync Connection › V1 › inputjson › connection_id › optionsGenerator

evidence.quote: The code reads only fields and system keys, such as hookUrl, performsubscribe or scheduledTime.

findings.avoid: Do not rename the key connection_id and do not edit the mapped component listFivetranConnections; change only the field's source / optionsGenerator, then re-save so dependsOn regenerates as []. Alternative if group filtering is wanted: add an optional Group dropdown as the first field, as List Connections already does.
findings.expectedResult: The Connection dropdown loads on open with no parent value and lists connections across all groups.
findings.verify: Dry run the connection_id source with empty input on a Fivetran account that has connections; open each action in the editor and confirm the dropdown loads.

findings.title: Get Connection and List Connections should be one LIST action with a mode
findings.location: Actions › Get Connection and Actions › List Connections
findings.issue: Two actions do one job (read connections). Users must pick between them, and Get Connection duplicates List Connections' lookup by id.

evidence.ref: Get Connection › V1 › perform (GET /connections/{id}) and List Connections › V1 › perform (GET /connections)
evidence.quote: two separate actions, no mode field in either inputjson
Always combine listing ("List All"), searching (by specific identifiers), "Search by ID", and "Advance Search" (if supported) into a single LIST action using a Mode selector.

fix.content: Add a Mode dropdown (List All / Search by Schema Name / Search by ID) to List Connections; show group_id/limit/cursor only for List All, schema for Search by Schema Name, and the connection dropdown for Search by ID (GET /connections/{id}, keeping the existing 404 -> 'No data found.' handling). Then retire Get Connection.

findings.avoid: Do not delete Get Connection once it is published or used in flows; it is unpublished with 0 runs today, so merging now is non-breaking.
findings.expectedResult: One action reads connections in every way the two do today.
findings.verify: Dry run each mode: list all, search by schema, search by id, unknown id (expect 'No data found.').

findings.title: List Connections and Get Sync History return only one page
findings.location: <action> › V1 › perform (single axios.get, no loop) and inputjson (no 'Enable Pagination' toggle)
findings.issue: Users get at most one page (default 100) unless they copy next_cursor into a second run by hand. The response does expose next_cursor and has_more, so nothing is hidden, but the KB requires the action to fetch everything when paging is off.

evidence.quote: const response = await axios.get(`${BASE}/connections`, { params, ... }); return { data: items, next_cursor: ..., has_more: ... }
if Mode is 'List All' ... and "Enable Pagination" is disabled, the perform code must automatically iterate through all pages (internal pagination) to return all records.

fix.content: Add an 'Enable Pagination' boolean; when off, loop on data.next_cursor (limit 1000 per page) and return the combined list; when on, keep today's single-page behaviour with limit/cursor inside an input group shown only when it is true. Cap the loop and respect the API rate limit.

findings.avoid: Do not loop without a page cap or without a delay on 429; do not rename the existing limit and cursor keys.
findings.expectedResult: With pagination off, the action returns every connection / sync in the range.
findings.verify: On an account with more than 100 connections, run with pagination off and compare the count with the Fivetran dashboard.

findings.title: Triggers pass the raw nested webhook body through
findings.location: <trigger> › V1 › modifytriggerdata (last line: return body;) and sampledata
findings.issue: Event details sit under a nested data object (data.status, data.sync_type, data.message), so later steps map data.status instead of a plain field.

evidence.ref: New Sync Completed › V1 › modifytriggerdata and sampledata
perform-code.md › Instant Trigger Perform Code (Modify data before send to flow) Rules
evidence.quote: Webhook data contains nested object format. Now need to flatten the nested object and return it to the flow as a flat object.

findings.avoid: Update sampledata to the same flat shape in the same change (plug-review.md check 15: the sample must match a live event). Do it before publishing: after publish, flows depend on the shape.
findings.expectedResult: Flows see status, sync_type, message, testName at the top level next to event, connector_id and connector_name.
findings.verify: Send a test webhook for each event and compare the trigger output with the saved sample.

findings.title: Re-sync tables are typed as one comma-separated string
findings.issue: Users must type schema.table pairs in an exact format; a typo is caught only at run time (the code throws 'Invalid table').

evidence.quote: "type":"string", "help":"Enter tables as schema.table separated by commas (public.orders, public.users)..."
Fixed choices are dropdowns, lists are repeating input groups, and nested objects are input groups.

fix.content: Replace tables with a repeating input group of two fields (Schema, Table), keeping the perform code's scope-building loop; exact JSON per dh-Input-fields-json-builder.md 'Input Group Static JSON Schema' (not fetched in this audit).

findings.avoid: Keep accepting the old string for anyone who already mapped it; do not rename the key tables, add the group under a new key.
findings.expectedResult: Users add one row per table; no format to remember.
findings.verify: Run with one row, two rows in the same schema, two schemas, and none (expect a full re-sync).

findings.title: Sync Connection always sends force: false
findings.location: Sync Connection › V1 › perform › const payload = ...
findings.issue: When the user leaves Force Restart empty, the request still carries force: false. This is harmless if false is the API default, which could not be checked here.

evidence.quote: const payload = force === true || force === 'true' ? { force: true } : { force: false };

fix.content:
-    const payload = force === true || force === 'true' ? { force: true } : { force: false };
+    const payload = force === true || force === 'true' ? { force: true } : force === false || force === 'false' ? { force: false } : {};

findings.avoid: Do not drop an explicit No: a user who picks No should still send force: false.
findings.expectedResult: An unfilled Force Restart sends an empty body; an explicit No still sends false.
findings.verify: Run with the field omitted, Yes and No and compare the request bodies.
